SMTO-UI-0064 — Current password is incorrect

GUID: d27f936c-8383-5f54-ae87-456328778943
Slug: portal-password-rejected
Domain: UI · Subsystem: authentication

What happened

  • The password you typed in Current password doesn't match your account, so SMTO didn't change your password. Your existing password still works.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Current password, type the password you used to sign in today, or the temporary password your administrator gave you. SMTO only changes your password after confirming you know the existing one.
  2. Type your new password in New password and Confirm new password, then select Change password. Both new-password boxes must match before SMTO sends the change.
  3. If you've forgotten your current password, ask your administrator to use Reset password on the Users page. A reset gives you a temporary password that you can then replace with your own.

What success looks like

  • SMTO confirms the change, and your next sign-in works with the new password.

If it still fails

  • Don't keep guessing: after several wrong tries SMTO pauses password changes for about a minute. Ask your administrator to reset your password. Never put passwords or browser cookies in an error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Current password is incorrect.

What this means

  • The account owner rejected the supplied current password before applying a change. The rejected request did not replace the saved password.

Why this can happen

  • The account owner rejected the supplied current password before applying a change.

How to diagnose it

  • The password change is confirmed, and your next sign-in accepts the new password.

How to fix it

  • The account store raised LoginDenied('Current password is incorrect.') and /auth/password returned 400 (not 401, so the page doesn't treat it as an expired sign-in); the saved password was not replaced. Resubmit with the correct current password, or have an administrator use Reset password on the Users page (/user) to issue a temporary one.
  • Enter your current password again, then submit the new password. If you no longer know it, ask an administrator to reset it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Enter your current password again, then submit the new password. If you no longer know it, ask an administrator to reset it.

How to verify the fix

  • The password change is confirmed, and your next sign-in accepts the new password.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Authentication guidance never changes account permissions or replays task work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
